# Changelog

Published versions of `@runablehq/managed-auth`. Agents updating or debugging a generated app:
find the app's installed version in its `package.json`, then apply the migration steps between it
and the version the current docs assume.

## 0.6.0

One client for every browser-context runtime: `managedAuthClient` picks the right sign-in flow
itself, and the desktop-specific client is gone.

### Breaking

- Removed `managedAuthDesktopClient` and the `/desktop` entry. Migration: replace
  `desktop ? managedAuthDesktopClient(config) : managedAuthClient(config)` (or any direct
  `managedAuthDesktopClient(...)` use) with `managedAuthClient(config)` from
  `@runablehq/managed-auth/client` — it detects the Electron bridge (`window.managedAuth`,
  exposed by the app's preload script) per call and runs the system-browser + deep-link flow when
  present, the popup/redirect flow otherwise. The explicit `bridge`/`redirectTarget` config
  options went with it: the bridge is injected only via `window.managedAuth`, and the dev
  redirect target rides the bridge (`getRedirectTarget`). Import the `DesktopBridge` type from
  `@runablehq/managed-auth/client` or `/desktop/preload`.

## 0.5.0

The Electron main-process and preload halves of managed auth now ship in the package instead of
living as template-managed files in each generated app.

### Added

- `@runablehq/managed-auth/desktop/main` — `createManagedDeepLinks({ applicationId, getWindow })`
  registers the `runable-<applicationId>` protocol (packaged and unpackaged variants), delivers
  macOS `open-url` deep links to the renderer (buffered until the first window loads), registers
  the `managed-auth:*` IPC handlers (http/https-guarded `shell.openExternal`, dev redirect
  target), and runs a localhost loopback relay in unpackaged runs so dev sign-in no longer
  depends on unreliable macOS scheme dispatch. It registers mechanism only: the app keeps the
  single-instance lock and lifecycle, forwarding second-instance and cold-start argv through the
  returned `handleArgv(argv)`.
- `@runablehq/managed-auth/desktop/preload` — `createManagedAuthBridge()` builds the
  `DesktopBridge`; the app exposes it itself
  (`contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("managedAuth", createManagedAuthBridge())` — the key
  `managedAuthDesktopClient` reads by default). Must be bundled into the preload script (preloads
  are sandboxed) or run with `sandbox: false`.
- `DesktopBridge.getRedirectTarget()` (optional) — carries the dev relay URL to the renderer;
  `managedAuthDesktopClient` resolves the deep-link target as
  `config.redirectTarget` → `bridge.getRedirectTarget()` → registered scheme.

### Changed

- `managedAuthDesktopClient`'s `bridge` is now optional, defaulting to `window.managedAuth`.
  Passing an explicit bridge still works, so 0.4.0 renderer code is unaffected.

## 0.4.0

Managed sign-in now works on every app surface: web, Expo/React Native (Expo Go, standalone
builds, Expo Web), and Electron.

### Breaking

- `issuer` is required in every config (`managedAuthClient`, `managedAuthExpoClient`,
  `managedAuthDesktopClient`, `runableManagedAuth`). There is no default broker anymore — omitting
  it used to silently target the production broker. Migration: pass the injected value — web reads
  `import.meta.env.VITE_RUNABLE_AUTH_ISSUER`, the server reads
  `process.env.VITE_RUNABLE_AUTH_ISSUER`, Expo reads
  `Constants.expoConfig.extra.runableAuthIssuer`.
- Removed `createManagedAuthClient`. Integrate through the Better Auth client plugin on every
  platform: `createAuthClient({ plugins: [managedAuthClient({ … })] })`, then
  `authClient.managedAuth.signIn({ provider })`.
- Removed the client `baseUrl`/`basePath` options. The exchange now goes through the Better Auth
  client itself, so its `baseURL`/`basePath` are the single source of the app-server address (on
  web they default to the page origin; native and desktop must set `baseURL` explicitly).

### Added

- `@runablehq/managed-auth/native` — `managedAuthExpoClient` for Expo apps: system auth session
  (`expo-web-browser`), SecureStore token storage, deep-link return, and Expo Web delegation to
  the web transport. Peers (all bundled in Expo Go): `expo-web-browser`, `expo-secure-store`,
  `expo-linking`, `expo-crypto`.
- `@runablehq/managed-auth/desktop` — `managedAuthDesktopClient` for Electron renderers over an
  injected `{ openExternal, onDeepLink }` preload bridge: sign-in runs in the system browser and
  completes via the app's derived custom protocol (`runable-<applicationId>` — the only scheme the
  broker validates). Unpackaged (dev) shells should pass `redirectTarget` pointing at a localhost
  loopback relay instead — macOS scheme dispatch is unreliable when several dev Electrons share a
  bundle id (see the playground's `desktop/main.mjs` for the pattern).
- PKCE (S256) on the native and desktop legs: clients send `code_challenge` to `/start`, the
  broker stamps `pkce_s256` into the identity JWT, and `/managed/exchange` requires the matching
  `codeVerifier` — an intercepted deep-link fragment alone can't be redeemed.
- Broker: delivery to custom-scheme redirect targets (`exp://…`, `runable-<appId>://…`) preserving
  their full path; https targets keep origin-root delivery.

## 0.3.2

Baseline: web-only client (`managedAuthClient` popup/redirect plus the framework-agnostic
`createManagedAuthClient`), server exchange plugin, broker. `issuer` optional, defaulting to the
production broker.
